title: Actor boundary claims and delegation model for RBAC v2 (resource hierarchy, scoped permissions)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an actor-boundary claims and delegation model for RBAC v2 to support hierarchical resources, per-scope permissions, and delegation tokens. This ticket captures the proposed schema for role/claim provenance, the runtime contract for decision evaluation, revocation semantics, and a migration path from the legacy RBAC surface. Goal is to provide an explainable, cache-friendly authorization path that preserves audit context for downstream logging and supports delegated short-lived privileges for integrations (webhooks, bots, CI runners).

Background:
- Current RBAC implementation conflates role assignment and resource scoping which makes explainability and incremental migration difficult.
- Several customers require delegation for cross-tenant agents and fine-grained short-lived access without creating long-lived service accounts.
- We need clear auditability: every decision must attach a provenance chain (actor -> delegation -> role -> scope) so Console and audit logs can surface why access was granted.

Scope of this ticket:
- Role/Claim model: canonical claim structure with provenance, issuance_time, expiry, and parent_claim ids.
- Delegation tokens: signed, short-lived bearer tokens with minimal surface for forced-revocation and audit context.
- Scope resolution: algorithm to resolve permissions from resource hierarchy, including inheritance, overrides, and deny precedence.
- Explainability API: deterministic explanation object returned with auth decision for UI and logs.
- Migration controls: backward-compatible endpoints and a canary rollout for runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical claim JSON schema and publish spec in Confluence: includes fields (actor_id, principal_type, issued_by, issued_at, expires_at, parent_ids, roles, scopes, metadata)
Implement runtime evaluator that returns {allowed: bool, explanations: [string], provenance_id: string} within 3ms p95 on auth cache hit for simple lookup
Delegation tokens implemented as signed JWT-like artifacts with opaque IDs that support forced revocation via revocation list and immediate audit entries
Migration plan documented with feature flag for 'rbac_v2_claims' and automated transformation job for existing role bindings
E2E tests covering hierarchical inheritance (ancestor grant, descendant deny), temporal expiration, and cross-tenant delegation
Dashboard panels show per-request auth decision and provenance id for 30 days retention in Console (canary)
decisions: Use immutable claim objects (signed) to capture the provenance chain; store only claim IDs in primary DB to avoid large payload duplication
Deny rules take precedence over grants at the same scope level; explicit deny cannot be overridden by ancestor grants
Authorization evaluator returns an explainability object; we avoid returning sensitive metadata in the API by redacting on a per-field allowlist
Delegation tokens will be short-lived (default 15 minutes) and include a revocation-id for immediate invalidation by listing in Redis
Cache: cache positive/negative decisions keyed by (principal_id, resource_id, action, effective_scope_version) with TTL tied to claim expiry
tradeoffs: Performance vs Explainability: embedding full provenance into each auth response increases payload size and serialization cost — we opted to return a small explanation plus a provenance_id that links into the audit store for full trace
Revocation model: polling revocation lists (fast) vs pushing invalidation events (complex). We start with revocation list + short token TTL to balance complexity and responsiveness

Storage: storing full claim objects in primary DB simplifies querying but increases storage and replication cost. We store claims in object storage and surface IDs in the main DB to reduce write amplification
implementation_plan: Spec: finalize canonical claim schema and publish at https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/rhac/claims-v2 (draft)
Schema migration: add 'claim_id' column to role_bindings table and backfill with transformer job (safe migrational mode)
Runtime: implement evaluator as a standalone microservice (auth-eval) behind internal gRPC with feature flag gating
Delegation: implement token issuer service and revocation-list service (Redis-based) with API for Console to revoke
SDKs: extend server-side SDKs to accept delegation tokens and to call explainability endpoint
Rollout: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% across regions with automated health checks on auth latency and decision drift
tests_and_monitoring: Unit: schema validation, scope resolution unit tests for 10k synthetic resource trees
Integration: end-to-end flow including token issuance, delegation chaining (2 levels), and forced revocation
Perf: auth-eval p95 < 5ms on cached decisions, p95 < 20ms cold (no cache) on standard instance
Monitoring: dashboards for auth latency, cache hit rate, number of delegation tokens issued, revocation-list size
Alerting: page on (auth-eval error rate > 0.5% for 5m) or (cache hit rate < 50% for 10m after expected warm-up)
